# Results — Study 812 (Corwin-Schultz Spread)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Corwin &
Schultz (2012): a stock's effective bid-ask **spread** can be estimated from its daily
**high** and **low** prices alone; that estimated spread proxies illiquidity, so a long
high-spread (illiquid) / short low-spread (liquid) book should harvest an **illiquidity
premium**. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's daily **Corwin-Schultz high-low spread** `S = 2(e^α−1)/(1+e^α)` (negatives floored at 0), then the **trailing-21-day mean** as the estimated spread, known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the estimated spread; **long the top 30%** (high spread, illiquid), **short the bottom 30%** (low spread, liquid), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| As-of | as-of 2026-06-30 — the last complete calendar month; no partial month in the stamped run |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled high-vs-low books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. The
illiquidity premium is documented as a **small-and-illiquid-stock** effect; a 50-mega-cap
survivor panel is exactly where it is *least* likely to appear — which makes a positive
result here notable, and the reader should treat the level as conservative in the sense that
delisted/de-rated names (often the least liquid) are absent.

**Estimator sanity.** The median daily Corwin-Schultz spread across names is ≈ **12.7 bps**
(cross-name median range 0.0–23.5 bps) — sensible effective spreads for mega-caps, and the
sort has real cross-sectional dispersion to bite on.

## The headline — long-high-spread / short-low-spread

Daily equal-weight top-30% minus bottom-30% estimated-spread sort (n = **4,125** days):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long high-spread − short low-spread)** | **+4.45 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **+3.24** |
| one-sample *t* | +3.06 |
| high-spread book / low-spread book | +10.64 bps / +6.19 bps (Welch *t* = +1.62) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | +0.76 |

The claimed edge **replicates, with the right sign.** The illiquid (high-CS-spread) names
*out-earned* the liquid ones by **+4.45 bps/day** (NW *t* = **+3.24**) over 2010–2026 — the
textbook illiquidity premium, and precisely the direction Corwin-Schultz + Amihud predict.
The pooled book Welch *t* (+1.62) is softer because the two legs' day-to-day noise is large;
the day-by-day long-short difference is where the signal concentrates.

## Placebo — is the relation a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the trailing-spread sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted**
panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+4.45 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.019 bps (0.916) |
| position of observed | **+4.88σ** into the right tail (right-tail p = 0.00000) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed +4.45 bps sits far in the **right** tail,
so the premium is a real property of the spread sort, not a lucky alignment.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,991) | +3.48 bps | **+2.03** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | +5.35 bps | **+2.52** |

The premium holds — significant in **both** halves — so it is not one era's artefact.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +4.45 bps | 2.14 bps | **+2.31 bps** | +1.59 | +0.39 | +5.8%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +4.45 bps | 10.14 bps | **−5.69 bps** | −3.91 | −0.97 | −14.3%/yr |

Here is the catch. At an **idealised** 1 bp one-way the book is still net-positive (+2.31
bps/day, ~+5.8%/yr) — but the *t* has already fallen to **+1.59**, no longer significant. At
a realistic 5 bps it turns firmly **negative** (−5.69 bps/day, *t* = −3.91). And the flat
cost charge is *generous*: the long leg is by construction the **illiquid** names, exactly
where a real desk's execution spread is widest — the very friction the premium is
compensating for. The gross premium is real; the net paycheck evaporates into its own
trading costs.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent per-name spread level that inflates the observed
high-low range (the Corwin-Schultz observation model) and — with `edge>0` — lifts the forward
mean. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.17** (sd 0.79), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.08`, seed 812) | **+10.09** (Welch *t* = +10.22) |

The estimator recovers the injected per-name spread with correlation **> 0.99**; the sort
recovers a *planted* illiquidity premium cleanly and stays silent on the null. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The Corwin-Schultz illiquidity premium **replicates on 50 liquid US
  mega-caps, with the correct sign**: long high-spread / short low-spread earns
  **+4.45 bps/day** (NW *t* = **+3.24**), significant in both eras (*t* = +2.03 / +2.52) and
  +4.88σ into the right tail of a 1,000-permutation placebo. A rare green on this desk — the
  effect survives even where it "shouldn't" (a mega-cap survivor panel). *Survivorship:
  current-membership mega-caps — magnitudes are an upper bound.*
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The gross premium is real but it lives entirely inside its own
  cost band. At an idealised 1 bp one-way it is still net-positive (+2.31 bps/day) but no
  longer significant (*t* = +1.59); at a realistic 5 bps it goes to **−5.69 bps/day**
  (*t* = −3.91). Since the long leg *is* the illiquid names — where real execution spreads are
  widest — the paycheck the premium promises is the same friction you pay to collect it.
